newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo Metal Ind plans larger capital spending.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo Metal Ind plans larger capital spending.

text.p: Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd said on Thursday that it plans parent company capital investment of 90 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1998.
This is up from a figure of 70 billion yen that the steelmaker announced early last month.
Sumitomo Metal said its actual capital investment in 1996/97 was 130 billion yen, up from 115.7 billion yen a year earlier.

Of the 90 billion yen planned for 1997/98, Sumitomo will spend 50 billion yen to build a new steel plant at its Wakayama plant in Wakayama prefecture, western Japan, to replace two existing steel mills at the plant.

The upward revision from the earlier forecast of 70 billion yen was mainly because of a decision to increase facilities for stainless steel production due to rising demand in Southeast Asia, a Sumitomo Metal spokesman said.
